I. Task A Geometry [16]
The planar fluid domain was constructed in SpaceClaim V22 from a rectangular outer boundary and a closed
NACA0012 profile. Upper and lower surfaces were joined by a finite trailing-edge segment. The aerofoil was rotated
clockwise through8◦ and aligned with the enhanced mesh. For inlet flow along+𝑥, this gives positive8◦ incidence
(Fig. 1). The leading edge is at(0.484,6.917)mm and duct corners at(±500,±75)mm.
Fig. 1NACA0012 geometry in the duct, with100 mmchord, 8◦ incidence, 1000 mmduct length and150 mmduct height. The
flow direction and aerofoil orientation define the aerodynamic incidence.
Fig. 2Baseline mesh with nominal 10 mmglobal sizing,2 mmaerofoil-edge sizing and growth rate 1.05: 7,687 triangular cells and
4,029 nodes. Minimum orthogonal quality is 0.186. The enlarged view shows refinement around the aerofoil; labels identify all
seven boundaries. Local refinement represents curvature and steep gradients, while smooth size transitions reduce abrupt resolution
changes. Near-wall suitability still requires assessment of the solved𝑦+ distribution.

B1: Solution method and convergence.
Cases 1–3 use S–A, standard𝑘–𝜀and RSM on the common baseline mesh, with SIMPLE coupling in double
precision. S–A employs its native near-wall formulation; standard wall functions are used for𝑘–𝜀and RSM. The first
crossing of all active residuals below10−3 is recorded separately from the final result. Additional numerical checks
target terminal residuals below10−5 and both force ranges, divided by the absolute window mean, below 0.1% over 100
consecutive updates. Runs that do not meet these additional targets are identified explicitly. The residual history is read
together with force monitors and conservation checks; each measures a different aspect of the numerical solution.

Interpretation of the wall treatment.
Standardwallfunctionsinferwallstressthroughalogarithmicrelation[ 1]. Strongpressuregradientscanviolatetheir
equilibrium assumptions. Low suction-side𝑦+ therefore identifies a modelling concern, rather than a direct measure of
force error. Values above 30 do not establish grid independence. Consistent refinement of wall pressure and integrated
forces is also needed; the enhanced comparison changes mesh and wall treatment together.
3

B3: Enhanced models.
EWT combines a two-layer near-wall formulation with blended wall functions[1]. The enhanced mesh contains
20,535 quadrilateral and 39 triangular cells. Hybrid-initialised RSM first crossed10−3 after 432 updates, with lift
172.65 Nand drag5.107 N; dissipation fluctuated near the threshold. Enhanced𝑘–𝜀crossed at 215 and met the stricter
targets at 753, with lift143.97 Nand drag15.611 N. RSM then continued from this𝑘–𝜀field without reinitialisation,
using Reynolds-stress relaxation 0.25 and momentum,𝑘,𝜀 and turbulent-viscosity relaxation 0.5. It crossed10−3 after
984 new RSM updates and met the stricter targets at 2,936. Different seeds and stopping accuracy prevent attributing
differences solely to relaxation, which changes iterative updates rather than the closure.

Data extraction.
Velocity magnitude was exported on vertical traverses at𝑥=0.05 , 0.10 and 0.20 m. Solid intervals were omitted
and native coordinates retained without smoothing. Surface pressure and𝑦+ were exported separately on each aerofoil
side. Total pressure and viscous forces were integrated over all three aerofoil walls, with unit span and directions(1,0)
for drag and(0,1)for lift. Incidence was not reapplied to these axes.

Discussion of comparison with the literature validation result [5].
The Sheldahl NACA0012 curve reproduced by Martínez-Aranda et al.[3] gives𝐶𝐿≈0.81 and𝐶𝐷≈0.017 at 8◦.
Estimated graphical reading allowances are±0.02 and±0.003, respectively, rather than experimental confidence limits.
TheReynoldsnumberinEq. (2)is3.21%below 3.6×10 5. Baseline𝑘–𝜀predictsliftwithinthereadingallowance,butits
drag is 5.30 times the central reference value. Enhanced RSM gives the lowest drag, still 94% higher, and overpredicts
lift by 24%. Agreement in lift alone therefore gives a misleading assessment.
The experimental and computational conditions differ substantially (Table 2). Close duct walls alter passage
accelerationandpressurerecovery. Chord-to-heightratioindicatesconfinement;itisnotablockagecorrection. Sheldahl
used two-dimensional inserts and end plates[4], so the finite span does not imply free wing tips. These reference data
must also be distinguished from the later paper’s own low-aspect-ratio tests. Neither experimental geometry nor its
transition conditions is fully reproduced here.

Comparison of the different CFD approaches attempted [8].
The common baseline mesh permits a controlled closure comparison. S–A transports modified viscosity,𝑘–𝜀uses
an eddy viscosity and RSM transports Reynolds stresses, allowing anisotropy. Greater complexity does not guarantee
greater accuracy. Enhanced mesh and wall treatment change together, preventing separate attribution.
Cases 2 and 3 retain continuity plateaus despite stable forces. Summed absolute cell mass imbalances, divided
by inlet flow, are 0.000105% and 0.000420%. These provide conservation evidence, but neither satisfy the stricter
residual target nor establish spatial accuracy. The S–A refinement results in Table 3 show a 4.79% medium-to-fine drag
change and non-monotonic lift. Grid independence has not been demonstrated, and an asymptotic extrapolation is not
justified[5].

Reducing the unmeasured inlet length scale from1 mto 0.01 m in baseline𝑘–𝜀reduces𝐶𝐷 by 32.8% and𝐶𝐿 by
5.99%; continuity still plateaus. This cannot calibrate an unmatched experiment. Reliability requires resolved wall
gradients, demonstrated mesh convergence, and matched confinement, inlet turbulence and transition. Stable forces and
residuals concern solution verification; validation requires physically matched measurements[6]. Both force coefficients
and pressure distributions must agree: compensating errors can produce plausible lift while leaving drag unsuitable for
engineering use.

Appendix AI usage log and guidance
Tool:Microsoft Copilot.
Date:During the week preceding 12 November 2026.
This declaration records three uses of AI assistance. The prompts below record the requests made for each activity. The
tool and date above apply to all three entries.
AI guidance table
Activity Scope of assistance
Learning to use the software Explanations of the interface, workflow and terminology; checked against taught material andsoftware documentation
Writing support Grammar, spelling and sentence structure of text prepared from the author’s handwritten draft;technical meaning retained
Figure code and formatting Presentation of the author’s exported Fluent results; original samples, units and surface identitiesretained
1. Learning to use the software
Prompt:“Explain in the simplest language, defining unfamiliar technical terms, how we should carry out this
coursework.”
Key response:Explained Fluent terminology and the roles of boundary conditions, turbulence settings, initialisation,
residuals and result export.
Howused:UsedtounderstandtheinterfaceandthesequenceofoperationswhenmovingfrompreviousCFXexperience
to Fluent.
Critical reflection:A general explanation cannot confirm the active case settings. The descriptions were checked
against the taught material, recorded Fluent settings and relevant documentation.
Modifications made:Generic explanations were made specific to the velocity inlet, pressure outlet, no-slip walls and
the turbulence models used in this study.
2. Writing support
Prompt:“Please use academic language.”
Key response:Suggested clearer grammar, spelling, sentence structure and more precise wording for the existing
descriptions and captions.
How used:Applied as language revision to text prepared from the author’s handwritten draft, retaining the procedure,
observations and qualifications.
Critical reflection:Smoother wording can inadvertently strengthen a conclusion. Numerical values and technical
meaning were checked against the recorded results; qualifications concerning residual plateaus, wall resolution and
experimental comparability were retained.
Modificationsmade:Removedinformalwordingandreferencestotaskinstructions;clarifiedthesequenceofoperations
and separated observations from their interpretation.
3. Figure code and formatting
Prompt:“The line in this figure overlaps the number 19.57 again; please redraw it using the data/figure in GitHub.”
Key response:Adjusted the annotation leaders and provided plotting and formatting code for the retained Fluent
exports.
How used:Improved label positions, legends, line styles, axis labels and the size of figures in the report.
Criticalreflection:Presentationchangescanobscuresamplesorassociatealabelwiththewrongcell. Checkscompared
the displayed values, native coordinates and cell identities with the retained exports; no smoothing or substitution of
result values was accepted.
Modifications made:Separated the 19.57 and 40.29 labels from their leaders, standardised the five-model legends and
retained the original surface and cell data.
